newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Two human rights workers killed in Colombia attack.
newsitem.headline: Two human rights workers killed in Colombia attack.

text.p: A suspected right-wing death squad smashed its way into a Bogota apartment early on Monday and killed two human rights workers and a relative, police said.

A one-year-old child escaped death by hiding in a closet. Police later found the baby boy sitting between the bullet-riddled bodies of his parents Mario and Elsa Calderon and his grandfather Carlos Alvarado. Alvarado's wife suffered multiple bullet wounds but survived.
The Calderons were university professors and also worked with a Bogota-based human rights organisation known as the Centre for Research and Popular Education (CINEP).
"We don't know what the motives for the attack were. It seems it was carried out by a paramilitary group," said Roman Catholic priest Father Fernan Gonzalez, CINEP deputy director.
"Police found the child in the middle of the bodies. He had hidden in a closet," he added.

Bogota police chief Gen. Teodoro Campo said five men armed with machine guns broke into the apartment in a middle-class district. They were dressed in black uniforms and posed as members of the Chief Prosecutor's Department, saying they had come to search the building, Campo told Reuters.
In another attack early on Monday in northern Colombia, a paramilitary gang raided a farm and killed eight peasants for allegedly collaborating with leftist guerrillas, police said.

The so-called Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba (ACCU), the country's most-feared paramilitary squad, is thought to have been behind the attack near the town of San Diego in Cesar province.

In a separate attack over the weekend, suspected ACCU members dragged three men from a bus, shot them dead and disfigured their corpses with acid in northwest Antioquia province, Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper reported.
Right-wing death squads and leftist rebels are locked in a bitter fight for territorial and political control over much of northern Colombia.
Scores of suspected leftist sympathisers have been killed in recent months and many communities have been transformed into virtual ghost towns as their inhabitants flee.
